purpose: Add longitudinal reasoning failure detection to every audit architecture without changing the underlying A-E topology.
sharedRules: Treat client first-person reports as privileged evidence about phenomenology and appraisal, but not as dispositive authority over cause, mechanism, importance, risk, or therapeutic centrality.

Keep salience, importance, and centrality separate. Do not drop a supported concern because the client calls it minor, and do not make a vivid recent event the organizing topic merely because it is salient.
Preserve established longitudinal targets across turns. New details update or challenge the target; they do not silently replace it unless evidence shows the goal changed.

Failure of one probe is not failure of the target. A nonverbal critic or presence must not receive invented dialogue; switch to triggers, body experience, action tendencies, avoidance, predictions, and consequences.

For divided or real/fake-self experiences, preserve differentiation or increased awareness that may integrate versus increasing alienation or expulsion as distinct hypotheses. Do not force healing, pathology, internal ontology, or external ontology.
When a later mundane example weakly fits an earlier high-stakes description, clarify why it counts and whether it is representative instead of resolving the earlier claim in either direction.
Before asking a high-information question, check the chronology and settled history. Re-asking known information is an audit finding unless the new comparison is genuinely different and necessary.
Give client-generated functional hypotheses priority as grounded hypotheses, not facts. Test concrete function, predicted protective outcome, and evidence that could disconfirm them.

If self-support or reduced self-rejection is an established target, preserve it without claiming it causes every symptom. Consider whether a less self-attacking capacity could perform any useful protective function only when that question advances the case.

Penalize both over-audit and under-audit: unnecessary alarm, blanket safety restrictions, irrelevant warnings, verbosity, needless rewriting of good responses, and failure to retain important uncertainty are all errors.
application: The experiment executor must append sharedRules to the generic audit taxonomy/rules visible to each applicable stage. This supplement does not reveal seeded truth, reference wording, architecture labels, or hidden open-question keys.
